old.text: Centre, along the bay · free — café-bar every 50 m Split's urban promenade, 250 m facing the bay, palms, café-bars. Touristy but useful: for an hour of watching, the city's rhythm passes here. Order a Pošip by the glass anywhere, watch the ferries leave for Brač and Hvar.

old.name: 🍷 Matejuška · evening · vin au gobelet
old.hook: Small fishermen's port · west of the Riva · evening — locals gather here with a bottle from the Pazar
old.text: Small fishermen's port · west of the Riva · evening — locals gather here with a bottle from the Pazar Matejuška is Split's small fishermen's harbor — at the western end of the Riva, where the boats line up on stone. No bar, no service: you sit on the stone blocks, bring your bottle from the Pazar (direct-from-producer wine, €5/L), a piece of pršut, a Kaštela tomato. It's Split's 7pm social ritual, off season. In summer, it's younger and denser.

linger:Matejuška with a bottle.brief: The old secret-gem: locals on the stone of the fishermen's harbour with a bottle. The '€5/L wine from the Pazar' is a claim: keep only if supported, else say 'a bottle from a shop'. Fife is a table card: name only.

old.name: 🍷 Plavac Mali — le grand rouge dalmate
old.hook: Pelješac · Dingač, Postup · descendant of Tribidrag — structured tannins, black cherry, garrigue
old.text: Pelješac · Dingač, Postup · descendant of Tribidrag — structured tannins, black cherry, garrigue Dalmatia's major red variety, a crossing descended from Tribidrag (Zinfandel) and Dobričić. Grown on steep slopes of the Pelješac peninsula (southern Dalmatia) — the two grand crus are Dingač (south-facing near-terraced vines, limestone, sea wind) and Postup (north-facing). Marked tannin, 14°+ alcohol, ripe black cherry, garrigue, sometimes animal. Producers: Grgić Vina (Mike Grgich, the Croat of Napa Valley who won the Judgement of Paris 1976, returned to make wine in Dalmatia), Saints Hills, Korta Katarina. Producers Grgić Vina · Saints Hills · Korta Katarina · Bura

drink:Plavac Mali.brief: Plavac Mali = Tribidrag (Zinfandel) x Dobričić (verify: parentage published ~2008?). The DNA DISCOVERY story (Kaštela, 2001, Carole Meredith, the nine vines) is the guide's food-history fold: do NOT tell it here, name it ('its story is told above'). Dingač and Postup. Grgić Vina is cut from this guide: do not recommend it.

old.name: 🍷 Pošip — le grand blanc de Korčula
old.hook: Korčula (island) · salinity, honey, apricot — Dalmatia's near-Burgundy
old.text: Korčula (island) · salinity, honey, apricot — Dalmatia's near-Burgundy Indigenous white grape from Korčula island, mostly grown at Smokvica and Čara in the island's center. Atlantic salinity despite the Adriatic, apricot, honey, sometimes wild fennel. Tank-fermented for fresh styles, barrel for top cuvées. Producers: Toreta, Bire, Krajančić, PZ Pošip Čara (cooperative). Open with seafood, brodet, soparnik. Producers Toreta · Bire · Krajančić

drink:Pošip.brief: Verify 'IGP since 1967' (it was Croatia's first protected white wine, 1967? verify), Čara/Smokvica.

old.name: 🍷 Tribidrag (Crljenak Kaštelanski / Zinfandel)
old.hook: Kaštela · ancestral grape — the original Zinfandel rootstock
old.text: Kaštela · ancestral grape — the original Zinfandel rootstock See the funfact. In the 1990s only 9 known vines remained in Dalmatia. Today, several producers are rebuilding the vineyards — Putalj (Kaštel Sućurac, 15 km from Split), Mihovil, Brkić. Generally more fluid in style than Plavac Mali, closer to Italian Primitivo than to California Zinfandel. Worth tasting for the historical curiosity as much as for the wine.

drink:Tribidrag.brief: This card is HOW TO DRINK IT TODAY: who makes Tribidrag/Crljenak Kaštelanski now near Split (Putalj in Kaštel Sućurac? verify), the name on the label, what it tastes like. The 2001 discovery story is the food-history fold: name it, do not retell. Wine labels In the glass · On the label · Ask for.

old.name: 🍷 Vugava — indigenous Vis grape variety
old.hook: Vis island · small production — rare grape, perfectly suited to the island climate
old.text: Vis island · small production — rare grape, perfectly suited to the island climate Indigenous white grape almost exclusive to Vis island (the most remote in Dalmatia). Gives structured, saline, slightly fat whites that age well. Very limited production. Reference: Lipanović, Roki's, PZ Vis (cooperative). A bottle to take home for lovers of niche whites.

old.name: 🍇 Prošek — vin de paille dalmate
old.hook: Straw-dried grapes · sweet · residual sugar — served with rožata or as apéritif
old.text: Straw-dried grapes · sweet · residual sugar — served with rožata or as apéritif Dalmatian sweet wine made from grapes dried on racks (passito method). Cousin of the Jura's Vin de Paille, Friuli's Picolit, Venice's Recioto. Varieties: Plavac Mali for red, Maraština or Bogdanuša for white. High residual sugar, 14° alcohol. Served as apéritif, at meal's end, or used in cooking for pašticada. The legal dispute with Italy over the «Prosek/Prosecco» name is ongoing — don't confuse them.

drink:Prošek.brief: Merge the old avoid card (Prošek vs Prosecco). Verify where the EU dispute stands in 2026. Wine labels.

old.name: 🌲 Rakija — eau-de-vie de fruit ou d'herbes
old.hook: Šljivovica, travarica, kruškovac · 40° — apéritif and digestif — whatever the house has on hand
old.text: Šljivovica, travarica, kruškovac · 40° — apéritif and digestif — whatever the house has on hand Balkan family of eaux-de-vie. Šljivovica — plum, the standard; travarica — herb maceration (sage, rosemary, thyme, wild fennel, up to 30 plants), Dalmatian specialty; kruškovac — pear; orahovac — green walnuts; medenica — honey. Served everywhere, at all hours, on every occasion. The Dalmatian peasant version sold by the maker holds its own. Decent industrial brand: Maraska (since 1899, Zadar). Buy direct from the producer or at the market.

drink:Rakija.brief: Verify Maraska founded 1899? (Zadar). Keep it short.
